Definition: from G4862 and G2227; to reanimate conjointly with (figuratively):--quicken together with.
BiblicalUsage: Paul says God quickened us together with Christ when we were dead in sins, and made us alive together with Him when we were dead in trespasses. The word is resurrection shared: Christ rose, and we rose with Him. It is the same act, counted for us.
TheologicalSignificance: The gospel in one verb — that is what this is, I believe: I was dead, Christ was raised, and His rising became mine.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
